settings.vibe: CRT glow, mall food courts, dial-up patience
settings.toneNote: the joke is never the 90s — the joke is how useless he is in them

concept.summary: Miles Okada, a present-day AI startup founder, wakes up in his fourteen-year-old body in 1996 — and discovers the time-travel fantasy is a lie. He can't predict a single game score. He doesn't remember which stocks matter or when anything happens. The only future knowledge that survived the trip is the stuff he actually loved at fourteen: every Tupac and Biggie track-listing, every movie twist, decades of pop-culture trivia. When his three best friends finally believe him, they appoint themselves his management team — and every scheme they invent to monetize a psychic fourteen-year-old is stupid, physically impossible, illegal, or socially fatal, because they are fourteen, have eleven dollars between them, and need to be home by dinner.

characters.name: Miles Okada
characters.backstory: Built a company on predicting things; now the only future he can prove is track-listings and movie endings.
characters.motivations: Matter in 1996 the way he mattered in 2026.
characters.flaws: Still pitches like a founder to people whose allowance is five dollars.
characters.need: To be fourteen with his friends — the thing he skipped the first time.

relationships.description: best friend since second grade; the first to believe him, the worst at keeping it quiet

characters.voice: startup jargon colliding with 1996 slang; keeps saying 'circle back' to kids on BMX bikes
characters.arc: From monetizing the future to spending an afternoon in the present.

characters.name: Reggie Park
characters.backstory: Has read one (1) issue of Forbes at the orthodontist and now speaks in percentages.
characters.motivations: Turn his psychic best friend into their empire.
characters.flaws: Every plan requires a car, a fake ID, or an adult — they have none of the three.
characters.want: Fifteen percent, off the top, of whatever this is.
characters.need: The friendship to survive being a business.
